name: New Zealand

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 267,710 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 263,310 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Excludes the Ross Dependency claim and the Realm states (Cook Islands, Niue, Tokelau).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 5,324,700). Low/high +/-1% for 2026 change and census revision. Everything inside ne:NZL.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2025 p.285 as quoted: 8,700 active. CIA Factbook 2025: ~8,800 Regular Force (4,300 Army, 2,100 Navy, 2,400 Air Force).

supportPersonnel.note: Active 8,700 (IISS 2025) minus infantry P roles (600 + 900). Covers navy (2,100), air force (2,400), artillery, engineers, logistics, staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to New Zealand in WWII (~200,000 served from ~1.6 million, over 10%); scaled down for a very small all-volunteer force. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. 1st Battalion RNZIR (motorised) on NZLAV and Bushmaster. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Army)

training.note: Rubric 0.75: small long-service professional force, Five Eyes/ANZAC interoperability.

count.note: Educated guess. 2nd/1st Battalion RNZIR plus NZSAS. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Army)

Educated guess. NZLAV: 105 bought, 35 offered for sale in 2010 (~70 remaining) plus 43 Bushmaster PMVs; NZ Army article gives no current totals. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Army)

training.note: Rubric 0.75: small long-service professional force, Five Eyes/ANZAC interoperability.

count.note: Educated guess. L119 105 mm light guns are the only artillery (NZ Army article, NZDF fact page); 24 is the commonly reported fleet. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Army)

training.note: Rubric 0.75: small long-service professional force, Five Eyes/ANZAC interoperability.

count.note: RNZAF inventory: NH90 TTH 8 + A109LUH 5 + SH-2G(I) Seasprite 5 = 18. MH-60R (5) replace the Seasprites from 2027.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: small long-service professional force, Five Eyes/ANZAC interoperability.

count.note: Active RNZN ships list: Anzac-class frigates Te Kaha and Te Mana = 2 (both upgraded with Sea Ceptor/CAMM).

training.note: Rubric 0.75 band minus: crew shortages laid up a third of the fleet (2022).

count.note: Active list: Lake-class IPV Taupo 1 + multi-role vessel Canterbury 1 + OPV Otago (laid up 2022-2026, returning) = 3; high adds the laid-up Wellington and Hawea. Replenishment ship Aotearoa excluded.
Educated guess. Very short-range air defence only (Mistral MANPADS historically; no SAM batteries). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Army)

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: competent joint HQ (HQJFNZ), proven in coalition peacekeeping (East Timor, Solomons, Afghanistan PRT); no independent large-unit command.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.75: small professional force with strong ANZAC identity.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5 average; retention problems in the Navy and Air Force.

weapons.note: Anchor 9: Javelin, Sea Ceptor (CAMM), P-8A with Harpoon/Mk 54; no strike fighters.

armor.note: Below anchor 9: no tanks, LAV III wheeled armour.

ships.note: Anchor 9: upgraded Anzac frigates with CAMM and modern combat system.

fortification.note: Anchor 8-9: no layered air defence; geography is the defence.

logistics.note: Anchor 9: new C-130J-30 (2024), Aotearoa replenishment ship, Canterbury MRV.

communications.note: Anchor 9-10: Five Eyes C4ISR, Link 16 on P-8A.

isr.note: Anchor 9-10: P-8A Poseidon (4), GCSB, Five Eyes intelligence; no drones.

air.note: Below anchor 9: no combat jets since the 2001 Skyhawk retirement; P-8A only.

cyber.note: Anchor 9-10: GCSB (Five Eyes) national cyber security centre.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. Rebased GDP 205,587,990,146 / population 5,324,700 = 38,610 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 256,824,472,388 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 205,587,990,146 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Series: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/NZL/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 1.10% of GDP in 2025. CIA Factbook 1.2% (2024), 1.3% (2021-23); 2025 Defence Capability Plan aims at ~2% within eight years (high).

industrialShare.note: asOf 2023: industry incl. construction 19.44% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS).

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Exports the large majority of its dairy, meat and fruit output; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 2,646,619 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 6.658% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 35,243. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook as quoted: 96,817 km total (2020), 64,957 km paved, 31,860 km unpaved (engineered gravel), 232 km controlled-access. Low is paved only.

railKm.note: World Bank 3,908 km (1998, low); CIA Factbook 4,128 km narrow gauge (2018).

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 22 ports, 2 large + 1 medium = 3 (Auckland, Tauranga, Wellington); 13 key ports named (high).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. New Zealand is below the 1 million GT threshold of the merchant-fleet table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_merchant_navy_capacity_by_country); CIA Factbook 2023 counts 117 merchant ships (2 container, 12 general cargo, 3 tankers).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Small deployable logistics; operations abroad rely on Australian/US support.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses (not from FAO data). Militarily irrelevant.

nuclearWarheads.note: New Zealand is a non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces. Nuclear-free zone legislation (1987); Treaty of Rarotonga party.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: isolated mountainous islands, local supply, population support; no harsh-climate bonus.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 data with 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:NZL (World Bank; Realm states excluded). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts: IISS Military Balance 2025 (personnel) as quoted; RNZAF inventory and active RNZN ships list; NZ Army article gives types but few quantities, so ifv_apc and artillery are grade D. No tanks, combat aircraft, submarines or drones: those roles are omitted. ships_major = frigates; ships_minor = OPV/IPV and the multi-role vessel. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D).
